model_interpretation.claim: A 32-lane X mapping makes each input-row access contiguous across a warp, while a four-output register window reuses Y neighbors and removes the baseline kernel's shared-memory/barrier path. This may improve coalescing and avoid synchronization, but trades the baseline's shared-memory reuse for rolling global loads; no speedup is assumed.

items.subject: Register rolling-window multi-output-per-thread kernel
items.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single kernel where each thread handles several consecutive Y outputs using a register rolling window, with warp lanes still accessing adjacent X values. Explore small output-chunk sizes to balance neighbor reuse against register pressure and occupancy. Do not use shared memory or extra launches in this track. For each neighbor coordinate q=j+d, match the supplied boundary convention: add 63 if q<0, subtract 63 if q>63, otherwise leave q unchanged. Preserve in-range index 63; do not assume endpoint planes are equal. Compute every output for varying signed inputs and preserve the supplied tolerance and buffer constraints. Validate with the oracle and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
